metadata.title: PCR-001: Standard PCR with NEB Q5 High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase
metadata.purpose: Perform high-fidelity DNA amplification for cloning, sequencing, mutagenesis templates, and accurate DNA amplification using NEB Q5 High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase (M0491).
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft for 25 uL or 50 uL high-fidelity PCR using Q5 Reaction Buffer, dNTPs, primers, template, and Q5 polymerase. Confirm the current manufacturer protocol, instrument manual, SDS, and local laboratory policy before bench use.
beforeYouBegin: Use high-quality purified template; plasmid or viral templates need far less input than genomic DNA.
Use the NEB Tm Calculator for primer annealing temperature because Q5 conditions differ from many Taq-based protocols.
Prepare reactions on ice, add polymerase last, and preheat the thermocycler to 98 deg C if following standard Q5 guidance.
Plan a no-template control and, when possible, a positive-control template/primer pair.

materials.name: Q5 High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase
materials.storage: Keep cold during setup unless the selected hot-start product explicitly supports room-temperature setup

equipment.name: Thermocycler
equipment.settings: Preheat to 98 deg C if following standard Q5 guidance

equipment.name: Microcentrifuge
equipment.settings: Briefly spin components and collect liquid at tube/plate bottom

tables.title: Run Record Template
rows: QC readout: gel band, Cq, melt curve, sequence, or colony screen
tables.note: Blank run-record template provided in the source PDF.

steps.action: Thaw reaction buffer, dNTPs, primers, and template on ice; mix each component and briefly spin down.
steps.criticalNotes: Keep enzymes and master mixes cold unless the selected hot-start product explicitly supports room-temperature setup.

steps.action: Prepare a master mix containing nuclease-free water, 5X Q5 Reaction Buffer, dNTPs, primers, and optional enhancer for all reactions plus overage.
Aliquot master mix into PCR tubes or plate wells.
Add template DNA to each sample tube; add water instead of template for the no-template control.
Add Q5 polymerase last if it was not included in the master mix.
Mix gently and collect liquid at the bottom of the tube or plate.
Run Q5 cycling with initial denaturation at 98 deg C, denaturation at 98 deg C, primer-specific annealing, extension at 72 deg C, and final extension at 72 deg C.

repeat.notes: The source specifies 25-35 cycles; no selected fixed count is given.

parameters.rawText: Initial denaturation at 98 deg C; 98 deg C denaturation
72 deg C extension; final extension at 72 deg C

steps.action: Use extension time based on amplicon size and template complexity; simple plasmid targets can use shorter extension than genomic/cDNA targets.

parameters.rawText: Hold at 4-10 deg C after cycling.

steps.action: Analyze an aliquot on agarose gel or proceed to cleanup/cloning if the product is specific; document polymerase, cycles, and primer sequences for sequencing or cloning.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Expected single band at correct size.

steps.expectedResult: Specific PCR product with a completed run record.

controls.name: No-template control
controls.description: Add water instead of template; it should have no visible product.

expectedOutputs: Single band at the correct size on an agarose gel.
No visible product in the no-template control.
PCR product for cleanup or cloning if specific.

troubleshooting.cause: Annealing too high, template issue, or inhibitor carryover.
troubleshooting.solution: Recheck primer Tm and template quality, and run a gradient or lower annealing.

troubleshooting.cause: Annealing too low or nonspecific primers.
troubleshooting.solution: Raise annealing temperature, redesign primers, and reduce cycles.
Increase template within NEB guidance, add enhancer, and extend time.

troubleshooting.cause: Too much template, too many cycles, or degraded DNA.
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce input/cycles and use cleaner template.

safety: Wear a lab coat, gloves, and eye protection; use nuclease-free tubes and filtered tips for setup.
Separate pre-PCR setup, template handling, and post-PCR analysis areas when possible; never open amplified qPCR plates in the clean setup area.
Use aerosol-resistant tips and include negative controls to monitor contamination.
